assertion: The cost of uncooked ground beef hit $7.16 per pound in August 2026, according to data from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics.
sql: SELECT series, "year", period, "value" FROM econ.average_prices WHERE series='APU0000FC1101' AND "year"=2026

assertion: Prices rose from $7.116 in July 2026 to $7.158 in August 2026, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics.
sql: SELECT period, "value" FROM econ.average_prices WHERE series='APU0000FC1101' AND "year"=2026 AND period IN ('M07','M08')

assertion: That marks a record high for beef prices, up from $6.631 a year earlier.
sql: SELECT "year", period, "value" FROM econ.average_prices WHERE series='APU0000FC1101' ORDER BY "value" DESC FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY
reason: Record applies to this ground-beef series (data from 1995), not all beef cuts; the series dipped to 7.062 in September.

assertion: Even though a price of a pound of ground beef was $6.50, most Americans say, 'I'm good with that. I want this protein for my family.' So they continue to buy.
speaker: Brooke Rollins
inaccuracy: The claim cites $6.50; BLS all-uncooked ground beef was 7.158 in Aug 2026 (100% beef 6.923), and $6.50 was the July 2025 level. 'Most Americans say' they are good with it is asserted with no survey.
sql: SELECT series, "year", period, "value" FROM econ.average_prices WHERE series IN ('APU0000FC1101','APU0000703112') AND "year" IN (2025,2026)

reason: Estimate/projection; the rise is small (about 0.5%) but its direction matches the claim.
